Django News Application
  • API reference

news.models

Database models for the Django News Application.

The models define role-based users, publishers, articles, newsletters, and the log entry created when an article is approved.

Classes

ApprovedArticleLog

A record created through the API each time an article is approved.

Article

A news article owned by either a journalist or a publisher.

Newsletter

A curated collection of approved articles.

Publisher

A news organisation that owns articles and can be followed by readers.

User

Application user with a reader, editor, or journalist role.

Details

class news.models.Publisher(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

A news organisation that owns articles and can be followed by readers.

Editors review articles submitted on behalf of the publisher, and journalists may submit articles under the publisher’s name.

Variables:

  • name (str) – Unique display name of the publisher.

  • description (str) – Optional free-text description.

  • editors (ManyToManyField) – Editor users who review this publisher’s articles.

  • journalists (ManyToManyField) – Journalist users affiliated with this publisher.

  • created_at (datetime) – When the publisher was created.

class news.models.User(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: AbstractUser

Application user with a reader, editor, or journalist role.

Extends Django’s AbstractUser. The role decides which pages and API endpoints the user may access. Readers can subscribe to publishers and individual journalists.

Variables:

  • role (str) – One of the values in User.Roles.

  • subscribed_publishers (ManyToManyField) – Publishers a reader follows.

  • subscribed_journalists (ManyToManyField) – Journalists a reader follows.

class Roles(*values)[source]

Bases: TextChoices

The account roles supported by the application.

classmethod from_db(db, field_names, values)[source]

Load a user and remember the role it was stored with.

news.signals compares the remembered role with the current one so the permission group is only rebuilt when the role changes.

clean()[source]

Validate that journalists do not hold reader subscriptions.

Raises:

django.core.exceptions.ValidationError – If a saved journalist account has publisher or journalist subscriptions.

Type:

property is_journalist

True if the user has the journalist role.

Type:

bool

can_modify(obj)[source]

Return whether the user may edit or delete an article/newsletter.

Editors may change any article or newsletter. Journalists may change only the ones they authored. Other roles may change nothing.

Parameters:

obj (Article | Newsletter) – The object to change.

Returns:

True if the change is allowed.

Return type:

bool

class news.models.Article(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

A news article owned by either a journalist or a publisher.

Exactly one of author and publisher must be set; a database check constraint enforces this. New and edited articles start unapproved until an editor approves them.

Variables:

  • title (str) – Headline of the article.

  • content (str) – Body text of the article.

  • author (User) – Journalist who owns an independent article, or None.

  • publisher (Publisher) – Publisher that owns the article, or None.

  • created_at (datetime) – When the article was created.

  • approved (bool) – Whether an editor has approved the article.

clean()[source]

Validate article ownership.

Raises:

django.core.exceptions.ValidationError – If the article has both or neither of an author and a publisher, or if the author is not a journalist.

class news.models.Newsletter(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

A curated collection of approved articles.

Variables:

  • title (str) – Newsletter title.

  • description (str) – Optional summary shown with the newsletter.

  • created_at (datetime) – When the newsletter was created.

  • author (User) – Journalist or editor who created the newsletter.

  • articles (ManyToManyField) – Articles included in the newsletter.

clean()[source]

Validate that the author is a journalist or an editor.

Raises:

django.core.exceptions.ValidationError – If a reader is set as the newsletter author.

class news.models.ApprovedArticleLog(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

A record created through the API each time an article is approved.

Variables:

  • article (Article) – The approved article (one log entry per article).

  • article_title (str) – Title of the article when it was approved.

  • approved_at (datetime) – When the log entry was created.

  • source (str) – Short description of what triggered the log entry.
